label: conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume
title: Complex-volume unification: binding $\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}$ and $\beta$-decay $\mathfrak{Q}_\beta$ are $\operatorname{Re}$/$\operatorname{Im}$ of one $\mathfrak{V}=E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M})$
html:
Conjecture. Complex-volume unification: binding \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} and \beta-decay \mathfrak{Q}_\beta are \operatorname{Re}/\operatorname{Im} of one \mathfrak{V}=E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M})

Conjecture (complex-volume unification of mass-binding and decay). [Lean classes: ComplexVolumeMatch / SingleFrakVAssembly / StageCSigma3Lift] Binding and the \beta-decay Q-value form the real and imaginary parts of a single complex fibre observable — the complexified mass-endomorphism convolution-defect

  \mathfrak{V}(K)\;=\;E_0\,\mathrm{tr}_M\big((\Pi_{\text{free}} - \mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}\big)
  \;\in\;\mathbb{C},
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}(K) = \mathrm{Re}\mathfrak{V}(K),
  \quad
  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(K) = \mathrm{Im}\mathfrak{V}(K),

the QOU analogue of the Neumann–Zagier complex volume \mathbb{V}(K) = \mathrm{Vol}(K) + i\,\mathrm{CS}(K).

The one object

Categorically — no braid words. For a confined knot K:

  • \mathcal{M} = \mathcal{M}(K) \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(X_K) forms the mass endomorphism of the object X_K representing K in the rigid monoidal category \mathbf{C}.
  • \mathrm{tr}_M : \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(X_K) \to k provides the categorical Markov trace (the closed/categorical trace; the fibre functor \tau is a different object, never \mathrm{tr}_M).
  • \Pi_{\text{free}} \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(X_K) provides the idempotent projector (\Pi_{\text{free}}^2 = \Pi_{\text{free}}) onto the factorized sub-object X_K \twoheadrightarrow X_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes X_c — the constituents un-linked (the categorical projection onto the split tensor: the same R-matrix braiding with the inter-constituent confining crossings dropped).

The convolution-defect measures the categorical trace of the part of \mathcal{M} that does not survive \Pi_{\text{free}} — a projection defect (no words, no overloaded \Delta, no new trace-like symbol):

  \mathrm{tr}_M\big((\Pi_{\text{free}}-\mathbf{1})\circ\mathcal{M}\big)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\Pi_{\text{free}}\circ\mathcal{M}) - \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{M})
  \;=\;
  \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\big(\chi^\lambda(\Pi_{\text{free}}\mathcal{M}) - \chi^\lambda(\mathcal{M})\big),

the per-partition object of the canonical binding (prop:categorical-mass-markov, binding_canonical). This describes any confined knot K. The nuclear binding case — a nucleus is a confined nucleon knot, factorized sub-object \mathfrak{p}^{Z}\otimes\mathfrak{n}^{N} — forms the physical instance \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathcal{M}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}}) of binding_canonical. Read over \mathbb{C} the defect carries one bit more information than either observable alone: its two bar-parities.

Forcing of Re/Im — the bar-parity = the complexification

Write q = e^{\lambda}, \lambda = \log q. The two crossing eigenvalues q, -q^{-1} split as

  \underbrace{\tfrac{q+q^{-1}}{2}=\cosh\lambda}_{\textbf{bar-even}},
  \qquad
  \underbrace{\tfrac{q-q^{-1}}{2}=\sinh\lambda}_{\textbf{bar-odd}},

so \cosh\lambda \pm \sinh\lambda = e^{\pm\lambda}. The bar-even and bar-odd parts constitute one element e^{\lambda} read on its two parities. Continue \lambda \mapsto i\theta (the substrate q rotated onto the unit circle / a root of unity) and \cosh\to\cos, \sinh\to i\sin: the bar-even/bar-odd split becomes a Re/Im split. That exactly constructs the complex volume:

real part (bar-even, \cosh, real q) imaginary part (bar-odd, \sinh, root-of-unity q)
Neumann–Zagier \mathrm{Vol}(K) (hyperbolic) \mathrm{CS}(K) (Chern–Simons)
QOU \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}(K) — binding / mass \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(K) — \beta-decay

The mass/binding channel provides the volume (real, \cosh) part; the decay channel provides the Chern–Simons (imaginary, \sinh) part of the same \mathfrak{V}.

Established results, and the fibre-level caveat

  • Proved (algebra). The bar-parity decomposition \tfrac{q+q^{-1}}{2}\pm\tfrac{q-q^{-1}}{2} = q^{\pm1} holds over any field. The complex reconstruction \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}+i\,\mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathfrak{V} follows from the two projection hypotheses (Lean, QOU.MassEndomorphism.ComplexVolumeUnification, 0 sorries).
  • Proved (classical limit). The free/factorized projection \chi^\lambda_{\text{free}} forms the disjoint-product factorization, proven at q=1 via Plancherel duality (conj:block-multiplicativity-v-free). The q-deformed case remains class-axiomatized (conjectural).
  • Conjectural (the unification itself). We conjecture that the physical binding and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta construct the Re/Im of the same \mathfrak{V} at a single normalization.
  • Fibre-level caveat (STRICT). At the archimedean / observable level \mathrm{Im}(q_0)=0 (lusztig_q_0_imaginary_part_zero): binding and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta both measure real numbers. The complex structure is therefore fibre-level (pre-\tau). \mathfrak{V}(q) provides a complex object in the fibre, and \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta provide its Re/Im shadows under different archimedean evaluations (real-q vs root-of-unity). There is no "complex mass" — there is one complex fibre object with two real observable shadows, exactly as \mathrm{Vol} and \mathrm{CS} are separately real.

The open single-\mathfrak{V} assembly and the \zeta_4-faithfulness constraint

The complex-volume model V_0(z) = \cosh z + i\sinh z satisfies the \zeta_4-partner relation: V_0(z + i\pi/2) = -\cosh z + i\sinh z, exactly negating the bar-even (binding) channel while keeping the bar-odd (Q_\beta) channel. The full \zeta_4-orbit decomposes the model into exactly the two faithful eigencomponents (trivial and sign isotypes vanish).

Constraint on the open assembly: Any candidate physical assembly \mathfrak{V} must be \zeta_4-faithful (supported entirely on the \pm i characters of \mathbb{Z}_4). A candidate with a nonzero orbit sum or sign isotype is falsified (QOU.Mass.ComplexVolumeZeta4Partner.SingleFrakVAssembly). This structural consequence forces \zeta_4^2 = -1 on the assembly, providing non-degenerate conditional content for the conjecture class.

The open Stage-C \sigma_3-lift obligation

The holomorphic tie hypothesis demands that a single Askey-Wilson three-term recurrence carries both the binding (bar-even) and Q_\beta (bar-odd) ladders. This implies the Casoratian W_k of the two ladders maintains a constant sign pattern forced by the recurrence parameters.

Constraint on the lift: The categorical \sigma_3-lift \Lambda \in H_4(q) of the decay operator must supply genuine c_4 rungs that satisfy this sign constraint (QOU.QBeta.StageC.StageCSigma3Lift). Any valid lift that leads to a sign-incompatible Casoratian W_3 \le 0 (given W_2 > 0) refutes the one-recurrence identification, serving as a parameter-free kill-test on candidate objects.

The S channel through \Phi_b (conditional wiring)

For the bar-odd S observable (S = c_3 + \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)), the conjecture's decay side takes the concrete form S(q_0) = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}\bigl(u(q_0)\bigr): the Chern–Simons part of the deformed complex volume at the substrate deformation u(q_0) (log meridian holonomy). The deformed volume itself is a theorem for 4_1 and explicitly computable via Neumann–Zagier; the two open inputs — the map u(q_0) and the channel identity — are carried by the class QOU.QBeta.PhiBSArgumentIdentification.SDeformedVolumeChannel. Composed with the argument identification of (algebraic-geometric dilogarithm equivalence), three statements are derived unconditionally from the two classes (phase_eq_im_deformed_volume, phiB_eq_cs_phase, exists_cs_vanishing): the fibre-branch \Phi_b phase at the identified argument is the deformed Chern–Simons part; the \Phi_b readout is the pure phase e^{i\,\mathrm{CS}(u(q_0))}; and if S flips sign between the anchors, that forces a substrate point q^{*} where \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}(u(q^{*})) = 0 — the deformed complex volume purely real. This last is conditional on a sign flip the data does not establish: each anchor value carries a CAL-3 propagated uncertainty of \pm 1.26 (130× / 32× the value); only the swing S(\text{muon}) - S(\text{proton}) is resolved (the cross-anchor c_3 difference, with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) cancelled). So it is a conditional structural statement, not an established prediction. This makes precise that \Phi_b touches binding only through this channel: remove the SDeformedVolumeChannel hypothesis and no binding statement about \Phi_b survives. On the open map u(q_0) itself, the Neumann–Zagier leading-form family laws are proved sorry-free (QOU.QBeta.UDeformFamilyPruning) over the corrected harmonic form \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak{V}(u) = (\sqrt{3}/4)(\mathrm{Re}^2 u - \mathrm{Im}^2 u) (cusp modulus \tau = -i\sqrt{3}, so the leading coefficient a_2 = i\sqrt{3}/4 is purely imaginary): all three candidate families — fixed-phase (\mathrm{Re},\mathrm{Im} \propto d), phase-crossing (\mathrm{Re} \propto d, \mathrm{Im} \propto d^{2}), and transverse-constant (\mathrm{Re} \propto d, \mathrm{Im} anchor-constant), with d = q - q^{*} — are refuted: each is even in d, hence the same sign on both sides of q^{*}, so none can produce a sign flip S(\text{muon}) > 0 > S(\text{proton}) were one present. The surviving necessary condition is that u(q_0) must cross the diagonal |\mathrm{Re}\,u| = |\mathrm{Im}\,u| between the anchors; u(q_0) itself stays open. The measured values live in the probe witness, never in the Lean, and — per the O2 analysis (docs/audits/2026-08-14-aomega-to-S-bridge-refuted-O2-negative.md) — the individual anchor signs are not resolved by the data; the resolved target is the swing S(\text{muon}) - S(\text{proton}), and the onward identification of this channel with the resurgent monodromy datum A_\omega is unsupported (no literature; integrality) and not carried.

Computational corroboration

The two channels construct distinct real components of one object: the E_0\cdot|\Delta(\mathrm{net})| net-route (the bar-even, binding-like E_0\cdot\Delta(\mathrm{tr})) provides a precision-ladder c_2 \approx -8.0, whereas the canonical c_2 = -1 lives in the bar-odd \mathrm{tr}_M brane-tower ladder (witness qbeta-ck-sseries-operator-match). Two different real c_2's for the two parities align with Re/Im components of one complex c_2.

Corollary — one story, and one proof

Conditional on the unification, the framework's mass/binding chapter and its \beta-decay chapter form one derivation: compute the complex defect \mathfrak{V}(K) once. Its real part yields every binding energy. Its imaginary part yields every Q-value. The "0.17\% \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residual" and the binding \Delta_\lambda gap become the same unclosed object — the imaginary and real parts of one defect — rather than two independent open problems.

Proof economy. A relation proved for \mathfrak{V} over a commutative ring R with the bar-involution \sigma (the structural setting — not \mathbb{C}) descends to both the bar-even (binding) and bar-odd (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta) parts from a single proof, because the projections x \mapsto x\pm\sigma x act additively. Formalised sorry-free in QOU.MassEndomorphism: invol_descent (one ring identity \Rightarrow both parity identities) and recurrence_invol_descent (a three-term \mathfrak{V}-recurrence with a bar-even multiplier c, \sigma c = c, yields the binding and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta recurrences at once — the c_k-ladder mechanism). The \mathbb{C}/Re–Im picture forms the archimedean instance (\sigma= complex conjugation).

Channel recurrences over categorical R, and the rotation between them

The two channels carry explicit three-term recurrences, stated in the same generic setting (commutative ring R with bar involution \sigma, never \mathbb{R} or \mathbb{C}; division-free via \sigma q \cdot q = 1):

  • even channel (compact / binding / continuous q-Hermite): H_{n+2} = 2x\,H_{n+1} - (1 - q^{n+1})\,H_n (evenStep);
  • odd channel (non-compact / \mathfrak{Q}_\beta / q^{-1}-Hermite), multiplied through by q^{n+1}: q^{n+1}\,h_{n+2} = 2x\,q^{n+1}\,h_{n+1} + (q^{n+1} - 1)\,h_n (oddStep).

The channel rotation is proved sorry-free (rotation_step). With a formal rotation element \iota \in R, \iota^2 = -1 (the fibre-level stand-in for i; Complex.I is only the archimedean instance downstream of \tau), a sequence satisfies the odd step at (q, x) iff its \iota-rotation n \mapsto \iota^n h_n satisfies the even step at the bar-conjugated data (\sigma q, \iota x) — the categorical form of the Askey/Ismail–Masson identity h_n(x \mid q) = i^{-n} H_n(ix \mid q^{-1}) [askey1989qhermite, ismail-masson1994]. Same eigenfunctions, rotated; one recurrence, two channels.

The operator ("rotation matrix") statement is split by provability. eigencolumn_eq_overlap proves generically that any eigencolumn of the channel tridiagonal operator has orthogonal-polynomial entries. The Leonard self-duality that would force those entries into the Askey–Wilson family [zhedanov1991, terwilliger2001] is carried as the conjecture class ChannelLeonardDuality. The bound \leftrightarrow free deformation-path reading (endpoints of one Askey–Wilson family, with the \mathfrak{V}-ladder riding one bar-even three-term multiplier) is carried as the conjecture class AWDeformationPath, whose two-channel descent channel_ladders is derived from recurrence_invol_descent. See the companion remarks rem:channel-rotation-askey-lit and rem:complex-volume-character-variety-path.

Archimedean specialisation. The measured binding and Q_\beta form the real and imaginary parts \mathrm{Re}, \mathrm{Im} of the complex Bring-surface volume, valued in \mathbb{R} (with E_0 : \mathbb{R}). This provides the archimedean readout of the generic complex-volume construction, acknowledged here.

Two further pieces of the operator picture are proved sorry-free at the free endpoint. First, the concrete AW(3) realization: splitting the channel tridiagonal operator into lowering, raising, and grading parts L, R, Q (the shift-split of multiplication by 2x at the q-Hermite bottom), the Zhedanov algebra degenerates to the q-oscillator relations

Q R = q\,(R Q), \qquad L Q = q\,(Q L), \qquad L R - R L = (1 - q)\,Q,

proved coordinatewise over generic R (chQR_rel, chLQ_rel, chLR_comm), with chM_eigencolumn_iff identifying the eigencolumns of L + R with the q-Hermite three-term rows; the odd channel satisfies the same relations at \sigma q by instantiation. Second, the Casoratian mechanism of the W-sign test: two solutions of one three-term step transport their Casoratian by W' = -B\,W (casoratian_step), and along a bar-even constant-multiplier ladder the channel Casoratian is invariant (channel_casoratian_const) — so a measured drift of the physical channel Casoratian reads directly as the k-dependence of the Askey–Wilson coefficient B_k. With c_3^{\text{even}} now measured exactly (witness qbeta-c3even-exact-sseries), the decisive W_3 sign test awaits only the c_4 rung pair.
